correctness.rationale: For r=2j−1, a nonunit gcd g with n is odd and makes mode k=n/g vanish. When r is a unit modulo 2n it permutes the residue pairs ±k, excluding 0 and n, hence permutes the absolute modal cosines. The product at every controllable site is therefore the endpoint product. The endpoint Krylov matrix is unit triangular because the unique length-t path to vertex t+1 contributes exactly 1; factoring out the common Vandermonde now gives |det K|=1 at every eligible site, not merely full real rank. The cosine product gives squared modal product (2n)^(−(n−1)), and the odd residue count is phi(2n). Reversing Krylov columns is the terminal input map, so integer surjectivity follows. The affine discrete spectral nodes stay distinct when b≠0; their first n monomials give a full-rank feature matrix, and the Vandermonde scaling gives b^(n(n−1)) at H=n. H<n is rank-deficient by column count. On each positive continuous interval the distinct exponentials give a positive-definite modal feature Gramian, including at zero damping. At infinity with positive damping, the Cauchy numerator cancels the modal-coordinate product by the endpoint Vandermonde identity. All determinants are full-state, including the consensus mode. RESULT.md lines 52–90 establish the unbounded claims. The frozen VERIFICATION.md and verify.py were inspected, not executed; their integer and small rational cases are supplementary, not a certificate for arbitrary horizons or sizes.
